name: Bilal Hasan
summary: An unbeaten 25-year-old flyweight (10-0, 1 NC), nicknamed 'The IndoNinja', and a former Cage Fury FC champion. He was born in Hawaii to parents who emigrated from Indonesia, grew up in Washington and looks to Demetrious Johnson for guidance (UFC.com). He won his contract with a 45-second TKO on the Contender Series on August 11, then knocked out Nilson Rojas in R2 18 days later at UFC Shanghai. He gets a main-card spot in his second UFC fight.

how_they_fight.Striking: A former Team USA junior taekwondo competitor (UFC.com). Against Rojas he kicked while Rojas boxed, hurt him with a body shot in R1, and finished him in R2 with a fully extended straight right as Rojas leaned in (Cageside). His Contender Series win came from a counter right hand (UFC.com). Eight KO/TKO wins.
how_they_fight.Grappling: Some, but little seen: he took Rojas down about two minutes into R1 and briefly got his back (Cageside). One submission win (R2, 2024, regional).
how_they_fight.Defense: Barely tested. He has never lost, and his UFC-level sample is about eight minutes of cage time across two fights, so his defensive numbers mean little yet. Rojas kept coming forward after being hurt.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: Finishes come early: four KO/TKOs in R1, three in R2, a submission in R2, and a KO in R4 of a five-round CFFC title fight (2025). His only decision was a split in his 2022 pro debut; Cageside notes he has not gone to the scorecards since. His other result was a no contest stopped after seven seconds (UFC.com).
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Has been a very heavy favourite: UFC.com called him the biggest favourite in Contender Series history. He said he wanted to 'take it super slow' but the UFC 'put me on a rocket ship' (Sherdog).

patterns: Counter right hand and straight right finishes
Finishes early: hasn't been to the judges since his debut
Fast turnarounds: three fights in about three months
concerns: Third fight in roughly three months (Aug 11, Aug 29, Nov 14)
Has gone past R2 only twice: the R3 debut decision and the R4 title-fight KO
A 15-minute pressure fighter like Gurule is a different test from short fights
keys_to_beat: Make him work for three rounds; he has rarely needed to
Pressure and clinch to take away his range kicking and counters
Test his takedown defense and his back-foot defense

news.text: Said he had wanted to take it slow, but the UFC 'put me on a rocket ship'.
Debuted 18 days after his Contender Series win and knocked out Nilson Rojas with a straight right at 2:28 of R2.
Won a UFC contract on the Contender Series with a 45-second TKO of Mridul Saikia.
Booked against Luis Gurule on the UFC 334 main card.
